def:
Header bits that a switch or other intermediate component is allowed to change while a TLP is in flight (for example the EP poison bit and certain Type bits), so ECRC computation treats them as fixed values.
Kid version: the parts of the label the post office may stamp on the way, so the sender's seal ignores them.
Where used: ECRC generators and checkers, analyzer ECRC verification.
Common confusion: computing ECRC over the header exactly as captured and declaring a mismatch.

exp: Data Link Control and Management State Machine
def:
The Data Link Layer state machine: DL_Inactive (no link), optional DL_Feature (PCIe 4.0+ feature exchange), DL_Init (flow-control initialisation, FC_INIT1 and FC_INIT2) and DL_Active (TLPs may flow). It reports DL_Up or DL_Down to the Transaction Layer.
Kid version: the sign on the bridge: closed, getting ready, open.
Where used: port design, link bring-up debugging, hot-plug.
Common confusion: treating LTSSM L0 as the same as DL_Active.

Optional bring-up step (PCIe 4.0 and later) in which link partners exchange Data Link Feature DLLPs to announce optional link features such as Scaled Flow Control; results are recorded in the Data Link Feature Extended Capability.
Kid version: the porters telling each other which extra tricks they know before work starts.
Where used: link bring-up, analyzer captures, Scaled Flow Control enablement.
Common confusion: treating its absence in a capture as an error.

Link Status bit that reports whether the port's Data Link Layer is in DL_Active, implemented on ports that advertise Data Link Layer Link Active Reporting Capable in Link Capabilities. Used by hot-plug and error-recovery software.
Kid version: the lamp that says the bridge is open for baskets.
Where used: pciehp, DPC and AER recovery, lspci LnkSta.
Common confusion: reading link training completion as the same thing.
